artists.biography: Jesus Jones are a British alternative dance band. The Wiltshire-based group, formed in late 1988, recorded and performed in the late 1980s, throughout the 1990s, and into the 2000s. They are best remembered for their track, "Right Here, Right Now", an international hit and subsequently globally appropriated for promotional and advertising campaigns. They are also well-remembered for the songs "Real Real Real" and "International Bright Young Thing."

Jesus Jones.biography: Jesus Jones are a British alternative dance band. The Wiltshire-based group, formed in late 1988, recorded and performed in the late 1980s, throughout the 1990s, and into the 2000s. They are best remembered for their track, "Right Here, Right Now", an international hit and subsequently globally appropriated for promotional and advertising campaigns. They are also well-remembered for the songs "Real Real Real" and "International Bright Young Thing."

release_name_discogs: Zeroes And Ones : The Best Of

perplexity.description:
Zeroes And Ones: The Best Of by Jesus Jones is a compilation album originally released in 2018, showcasing the British band's blend of electronic and rock music that defined their late 1980s and early 1990s sound. The album spans key tracks from their career, including hits from their breakthrough albums Liquidizer (1989) and Doubt (1991), which combined alternative rock with electronic dance elements. This fusion helped Jesus Jones stand out during the era, with singles like "Right Here, Right Now" achieving international success and critical acclaim for their innovative sound.

Positioned as a career-spanning best-of collection, Zeroes And Ones highlights the band's evolution and enduring appeal within the electronic rock genre. Released on Demon Records, the compilation serves both as an accessible introduction for new listeners and a comprehensive retrospective for longtime fans. While the band’s commercial peak was in the early 1990s, this compilation underscores their lasting influence and the continued relevance of their hybrid style. The album was well-received for its curated selection of tracks that capture the energy and spirit of Jesus Jones’ distinctive sound.
